watch_port_vale.title: Rochdale AFC suffers 4-2 defeat at Port Vale
watch_port_vale.excerpt: Rochdale AFC suffered a disappointing 4-2 defeat against Port Vale, with early goals sealing the match early on.
watch_port_vale.content_html:
Port Vale secured a convincing 4-2 victory over Rochdale AFC in a League Two match on Saturday, October 31, 2026. The game, held at Vale Park, saw the home side take control early, scoring three goals within the first 22 minutes.

Onel Hernandez opened the scoring just 90 seconds into the match, finishing a through-ball from Kyle Dempsey. Port Vale doubled their lead shortly after, with George Byers converting a penalty awarded for a foul on Hernandez.

The third goal came when Jordan Gabriel capitalised on a rebound after a shot from Dempsey was parried by Rochdale's goalkeeper Sam Waller.

Despite a brief threat from Rochdale, when Cian Hayes set up Dajaune Brown, the visitors struggled to find their rhythm. The second half saw fewer chances, but Ian Henderson managed to score for Rochdale in the 82nd minute.

However, Keyrol Figueroa restored Vale's three-goal cushion just minutes later, before Charlie Tasker added a second for Rochdale with the last kick of the game.

This defeat leaves Rochdale needing to regroup as they prepare for their next fixture. Manager Ian Watson noted the team's defensive lapses, stating that they conceded 'soft goals' which ultimately cost them the match.

Fans will be looking for improvements in their upcoming games to climb the League Two table.

fleetwood_preview.title: Rochdale AFC eliminated from Jersey Mike’s Trophy after 4-1 defeat to Doncaster Rovers
fleetwood_preview.excerpt: Doncaster Rovers manager Grant McCann has backed Sean Grehan following a challenging performance against Rochdale, highlighting the importance of bravery in football.
fleetwood_preview.content_html:
ONGOING STORY — Updated 5 November 2026 at 17:09 GMT. 31 source updates have been combined into this article.

Doncaster Rovers manager Grant McCann has expressed his support for young defender Sean Grehan after a difficult match against Rochdale in the EFL Trophy.

Grehan, who has been a regular starter this season, was substituted at half-time during the 4-1 victory over Rochdale after making an error that allowed Ian Henderson to score early in the match.

Despite the setback, McCann praised Grehan's potential, stating, "Sean's top. He's going to be top-class. I want him to keep making those types of passes. I want him to be brave."

McCann emphasized that mistakes are part of the game and encouraged Grehan to learn from the experience, reinforcing the importance of taking risks in football.

The match took place at the Crown Oil Arena, where Doncaster Rovers secured their third away victory of the season. The win was particularly significant following a disappointing 6-1 loss to MK Dons just days earlier.

McCann noted that the decision to substitute Grehan was partly due to managing his minutes, as he had played the full match previously.

Looking ahead, Doncaster Rovers will face Fleetwood Town in the FA Cup first round on November 7, 2026.

The team aims to build on their recent performance and continue their progress in the competition, while Grehan will be looking to bounce back and prove his worth as a key player for the squad.

Update timeline

  • 5 November 2026, 17:09 GMT: Grant McCann praises Sean Grehan after Rochdale error in EFL Trophy match
  • 31 October 2026, 10:18 GMT: Rochdale AFC eliminated from Jersey Mike’s Trophy after 4-1 defeat to Doncaster Rovers
